owned_invariants: The task is transitions, a list of at most 256 [state, label, state] triples of text. A task the host cannot read is refused before anything is asked. The declared states are those the transitions name.
One question is asked, the task as written. The reply is an object with claims, a nonempty list; each claim has a kind, difference or equivalence, and a left and a right state.

For claim k the host records claim<k>:states_declared, then claim<k>:witnessed (a difference carries a witness, an equivalence a certificate list), then claim<k>:separates (the witness holds at one state and not the other) or claim<k>:bisimulation (the certificate is a list of distinct pairs of declared states that holds the claimed pair, and every move of either state of a pair is matched by a move of the other with the same label into a pair of the list). A claim that fails one of these is not checked further and the others still are.

A formula is tt, ff, [not, f], [and, f, g], [or, f, g], [dia, label, f] or [box, label, f], nested at most 12 deep. The whole formula is read before it is judged, whether or not a state reaches a part of it. dia holds when some move with the label leads to a state where f holds, and box when every such move does.
The run is certified as CLAIMS_WITNESSED when every predicate passed, with the number of claims.
boundaries: A difference is shown only by a separating formula and an equivalence only by a bisimulation among the pairs given. A formula that fails does not show the states equivalent, and a certificate that fails does not show them different.
The host evaluates a formula over the finite system itself and never follows a claim of its own. Nothing a reply sends is executed.
The system is bounded at 256 transitions and a formula at 12 deep, so one claim costs a bounded amount of work.

score.level_basis: Typed refusals on every failure path, closed requests, exact unbounded integers and rationals, no float, no unwrap or expect.

basis.G1: Module header declares AuthorityEffect None and the contract URN; public items match this contract and code/rust/pfp_operads/README.md. Not B: no requirement-to-symbol trace beyond the README and docs/plans/operads_redesign.md.
basis.G2: Non-Numeric: states and labels are text compared as written, formulas are evaluated as sets of states, and the limits are usize bounds. The limits are asserted as the values 256 and 12, one inside and one outside. Not B: tested on examples, not proven.
basis.G3: Each unreadable task, claim and formula has its own reason, a formula that is not one of the seven forms or has the wrong arguments is malformed, and a claim that fails a predicate is recorded and not an error. No unwrap or expect, and no index. Slices are matched by pattern. Not B: panic-freedom is tested, not proven.
basis.G4: 25 WF17 tests assert the registry entry, the prompt byte for byte, a difference and an equivalence certified, the constants, not, and and or as written, dia for some move and box for every move, a formula holding at both states or neither, a state no transition names, a missing witness or certificate, a relation that is not a bisimulation, a certificate that lacks the claimed pair or repeats one or names an undeclared state, a move left unmatched or matched under another label, a failed claim not checked further, each malformed reply, claim and formula by its reason, every part of a formula read, the depth limit 12 and the limit of 256 transitions, and a deep formula over many moves. Mutation campaign R = 99/99. clippy -D warnings and rustfmt pass. Not B: mutants are hand-written one-line edits, not a generated campaign, and there are no generator-driven property tests.
basis.G5: Measured worst cyclomatic 9, cognitive complexity is not measured for Rust, nesting 3; ceiling A+, recorded A.
